title: Questions and short answers
tagline: Asking about people, places, times and reasons — the right word order every time.
why: Every Speaking Part 1 exchange is built from questions, and Reading Part 3 tests whether you can match the right question to the right answer. Get the order wrong — put the helper verb in the wrong place, or forget do — and it's hard for people to understand you.

hook.text: Sofia has a notebook. "Where are you from, Liam?" "Trujillo." "Do you play any sports?" "Football." "Who is your best friend here?" Liam smiles. "You, Sofia — you ask great questions!"
hook.ask: Look at Sofia's three questions. Which word comes first each time — and what comes right after it?

diagrams.title: How to build a question

steps.label: Start with the question word (if there is one)
Add the helper: be / do-does-did / a modal
Add the rest and the question mark

diagrams.caption: The helper always comes before the person — that's what makes it a question.

diagrams.title: Questions about the object vs the subject

sentences.note: asking about the place — needs do
who is the subject — no do, word order stays normal
with be, no do is needed

diagrams.caption: When who or what IS the person doing the action, the sentence keeps its normal order — no do.

use.point: Yes/No questions: be, do/does/did and modals go first

examples.note: did + base verb, not the past form
modals make their own questions, just like be

use.point: Wh- questions: about the object, place, time or reason
Questions about the subject: no do, no change

examples.note: who is the subject — the word order stays the same
what is the subject here, so no does
short answer = subject + the same auxiliary

watch_out.why: Wh- questions about the object need do/does/did — don't skip it.
does + base verb, not the -s form.
Questions about the subject don't use do — the word order doesn't change.

watch_out.wrong: How many money have you got?
watch_out.why: Money is uncountable — use how much, not how many.

watch_out.wrong: Yes, I do. (answering Are you ready?)
watch_out.why: The short answer repeats the auxiliary in the question — be needs am/is/are, not do.
The question word always goes first, not last.

l1.why: In English, the question word always starts the sentence, and the preposition moves to the end.

l1.wrong: How many years do you have?
l1.why: Age uses how old + be, not how many years + have.
English questions with a normal verb need do/does — Spanish doesn't.
When who is the subject, there's no do — the sentence keeps the normal word order.
You still need do/does before the subject and verb in a question.

remember.trick: Question word first, then the helper, then YOU!
remember.tip: Say the question word, then ask 'what helps?' — be, do/does/did or a modal — before the person.

dialogue.title: The school magazine interview
dialogue.context: Sofia is writing for the school magazine. She interviews Liam at lunchtime.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Hi Liam! Can I ask you some questions for the magazine?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Sure! What do you want to know?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: I'm from Trujillo. Why do you ask?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Just curious! How long have you lived in Lima?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: About two years. Who else are you interviewing?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Nadia and Mateo. Do you play any sports?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Yes, I do — football. How often do you write for the magazine?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Every month! One last question: what is your favourite subject?

practice.instructions: Put the words in order. Tap them one by one.

items.answer: How many brothers have you got?
What time does the film start?
Are you ready for the test?

practice.instructions: Right or wrong? Tap ✓ or ✗. If it is wrong, say the right sentence.

items.why: wh- question about a place, correct word order
question about the subject — no do needed

items.sentence: How many money have you got?

items.why: no do needed when who is the subject

can_do: I can make Yes/No questions with be, do/does/did and modals.
I can ask Wh- questions about people, places, times and reasons.
I can ask Who…? and What…? about the subject without do.
summary: Yes/No questions start with be, do/does/did or a modal.
Wh- questions about the object, place or time need do/does/did too: Where do you live?
When who or what is the subject, there's no do: Who called you?
Use how + adjective for details: how often, how long, how many, how much, how far.
Short answers repeat the same auxiliary as the question: Are you ready? — Yes, I am.
